Petitioner ample opportunity to defend himself. Thus, the aforementioned acts committed by the Petitioner workman 
squarely fall under the category of serious misconduct as defined under Clauses 19(a), (c), (d) and (e) of the Andhra 
Pradesh Shops and establishments Rules, 1990. 


Rules 19 (a), (b), (c), (d) and (e) of AP Shops & Establishment Rules provides as here under: - 

i. Clause 19(a): Willful insubordination or disobedience of any lawful and reasonable order of a superior. 
ii. Clause 19(C): Damage to the employer’s property. 

iii. Clause 19(d): Riotous or disorderly behavior in the premises of the establishment. 

iv. Clause 19(e): Threatening or intimidating any employee or superior. 


The misconduct committed by the workman along with employees of assaulting superiors, instigating others, and 
participating in the riotous violent activities constitute serious act of misconduct which strike at the root of 
workplace discipline. The act of workman causing grievous injuries to managerial staff is a grave and serious 
misconduct that is not condonable. Therefore, the dismissal order passed by Respondent against the workman is 
justified and appropriate action. 


13. Respondent has relied upon the few decisions of Hon’ble Supreme Court which are relevant to the point and 
discussed as here under: - 


(a) Hon'ble Supreme Court in Krishnakali Tea Estate Bharatiya Vs. Aknn Chah Mazdoor Sanah - (2004) 8 SCC 
200 upheld the dismissal of workmen who had assaulted managerial personnel causing damage to property, 
gherao of the management, wrongfully confining manager. The Apex Court observed that such violent Conduct 
cannot be taken lightly, and the punishment of dismissal was warranted to preserve discipline and safety at the 
workplace. 


(b) Similarly, Hon’ble Supreme Court in the case of Muriadih Colliery Vs. Bihar Colliery Kamgar Union - 
(2005) 3 SCC 331, held that the dismissal of employees who participated in a violent mob attack, causing 
injury to the General Manager, was justified, and interference by the Labour Court under Section 11-A of 
the ID Act was disapproved and the punishment proportionate to the misconduct. was upheld. 


(c) The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of M.P, Electricity Board Vs. Jagdish Chandra Sharma - order 
(2005) 3 SCC 401. of dismissal of a Workman who assaulted a senior officer, restored the decision of the 
Industrial Court, thereby reiterating that acts of violence by employees, particularly against their superiors, 
must be dealt with strictly and are not open to lenient treatment. The reinstatement ordered by the Labour 
Court was reversed, affirming the employer's authority to maintain discipline through dismissal. 


(d) In the case of Hombe Gowda Educational Trust Vs. State of Karnataka - (2006) 1 


SSC 430, the Hon’ble Supreme Court underscored the importance of workplace discipline and held that even 
provoked assault on a superior, amounts to gross indiscipline. The Court stated: "30. In view of the change in 
economic policy of the country, it may not now be proper to allow the employees to break the discipline with 
impunity. Our country is governed by the rule of law. All actions, therefore, must be taken in accordance with 
law.” 


(e) In the case of Usha Breco Mazdoor Sangh Vs. Management of M/S. Usha Breco Ltd — (2008) 5 SCC 554, 
Hon’ble Supreme Court while reaffirming the legal position laid down by it is in the case firestone Tyre and 
Rubber Co. Vs. The management and Others - (1973) 1 SCC 813, held: - 


“31. It is one thing to say that finding of an Enquiry Officer is perverse or betrays the well-known doctrine 
of proportionality another thing to say that only because two views are possible, the Labour Court shall interfere 
therewith. In other words, it is one thing to say that on the basis of the materials on record, the Labour Court comes 
to a conclusion that a verdict of guilt has been arrived at by the Enquiry Officer whereas the materials suggested 
otherwise but it is another thing to say that such a verdict was also a possible view. 


7326 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA NOVEMBER 29, 2025/AGRAHAY ANA 8, 1947 [PART II—SEc. 3(ii)] 


39. The upshot of our discussion is that the decision of the labour Court should not be based on mere 
hypothesis. It cannot overturn a decision of the Management on ipse dixit. Its jurisdiction under section 11-A of the 
Act although is a wide one, must be judiciously exercise either whimsically or capriciously. It may scrutinize and 
analyze the evidence but what is important is how it does so.” 


(f) Further, in the case of New Shorrock Mills vs Maheshbhai T. Rao, 1996 SCC page 590. Hon’ble 
Supreme Court held: - 


“35. In the case of New Shorrock Mills Vs. (1996) Maheshbhai T Rao 6 of SCC 590, held that: 


"Labour Court in the present case having come to a Conclusion that the finding of the departmental enquiry was 
legal and proper, the Respondents order of discharge was not by way of victimization and that the Respondent 
workman had Seriously misbehaved and was thus guilty of misconduct, ought not to have interfered with the 
punishment, which was awarded, in the manner it did. This is not a case where the Court Could Come to the 
conclusion that the punishment was awarded was shockingly disproportionate to the employee's conduct and his past 
service record." 


(g) The Supreme Court in the case of Northeastern Karnataka RTC Vs. Ashappa 2006 (5) SCC 137 reaffirmed 
that the Tribunal must not lightly interfere with the employer's disciplinary decisions and reiterated the "shockingly 
disproportionate” standard. 


(h) In Hombe Gowda Educational Trust Vs. State of Karnataka (cupra), the Hon'ble Supreme Court clarified 
that the days of automatic sympathy towards the workman are over, and that discipline must be maintained at all 
costs in light of contemporary industrial conditions. The Tribunal's power to substitute the employer's decision must 
be exercised with restraint. 


(i) In the case of Muriadih Colliery (Supra) & Krishnakali Tea 


Estate (Supra), the Apex Court expressly held that interference by Labour Courts with dismissal orders passed for 
acts involving violence and assault was not permissible under section 11-A of the ID Act, as the punishment was not 
disproportionate. 


Thus, in view of the principles laid down by the Honorable Apex Court as discussed above, there is ample 
oral and documentary evidence on record to substantiate the charges against the petitioner workman, and it cannot 
be said that the order of dismissal of Petitioner is perverse or shockingly disproportionate. 


14. As regard the plea of the petitioner workman that Respondent Management has victimize him due to the being 
member of the union and also for raising the demand related to welfare of the workman. 


In this context, Respondent has relied upon the decision of the Supreme Court in the case of Bharat Iron 
Works versus Bhagobhai Balubhai Patel, 1976 SCC page 518. Therein Hon’ble Supreme Court has laid down the 
legal test for establishing the plea of victimization as discussed here under: - 


"11. The onus of establishing plea of victimisation will be upon the person pleading 


it. Since a charge of victimisation is a serious matter reflecting, to a degree, subjective upon the attitude of 
the employer evidenced by acts and conduct, it has to be established by safe and sure evidence. Mere allegations, 
vague suggestions and insinuations are not enough. All particulars of the charge brought out, if believed, must be 
weighed by the Tribunal and a conclusion should be reached on a totality of the evidence produced." 


The Apex Court further held: 


"12. Once, in the opinion of the Tribunal a gross misconduct is established, as required, on legal evidence either in a 
fairly conducted domestic enquiry or before the Tribunal on merits, the plea of victimisation will not carry the case 
of the employee any further. A proved misconduct is antithesis of victimisation as understood in industrial 
relations." 


15. Thus, in view of the principle laid down by Hon’ble Apex Court, as discussed above the petitioner workman 
has failed to produce any evidence in support of the plea that the action of Respondent management in dismissing 
him from service is victimization of the petitioner workman. The petitioner workman has failed to discharge his 
burden of proof regarding plea of victimization or unfair labor practices hence same is untenable. 


16. As regard the plea of the petitioner that they he has been acquitted from the criminal trial by court in respect of 
the alleged acts of misconduct. In this context, the decision of Honorable Supreme Court in the case of Deputy 
Inspector General of Police versus Sethu . Thiruvan, 2013 SCC page 598 is relevant, wherein Honorable Apex Court 
have held that mere acquittal in a criminal trial does not nullify or override the finding of a valid domestic inquiry. 
Further, Honorable Apex Court held that the standard of proof in a criminal trial is proof beyond reasonable doubt, 
whereas in a domestic inquiry it is only preponderance of the probability. 


[भाग 1--खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : नवम्बर 29, 2025/अग्रहायण 8, 1947 7327 


In the case of Commissioner of Police vs Narendra Singh, 2006 SCC page 265, Honorable Apex Court 
held that the disciplinary proceeding can proceed independently and that an employee can be dismissed from service 
based on finding of a department inquiry even if no conviction is recorded in the criminal trial. The finding in the 
inquiry against the workman is based on credible evidence, including eyewitness testimonies and documentary 
records and same does not warrant any interference. 


17. Hon’ble Supreme Court in the case of Employers Management West Bokaro Gallery Colly of TISCO Limited 
vs Concern Workman Ram Prakash Singh, 2008 LLR, page 432, 


“16. In U.P State Road Transport Corporation Vinod Kumar, 2007 (13) SCALE 690 this Court again observed that 
in the absence of a challenge to the legality or fairness of the domestic enquiry the Court should be reluctant to 
either interfere with the finding recorded by the Enquiry officer or the punishment awarded by the Punishing 
Authority. 


17. After going through the order of the industrial Tribunal, were are of the opinion that the Tribunal has interfered 
with the findings recorded by the domestic. Tribunal as if it was the appellate Tribunal. There was evidence present 
on record regarding indecent riotous and disorderly behavior of the Respondent towards his superiors. The 
management witness who were present at the scene of occurrence have unequivocally deposed about the 
misbehavior of the Respondent towards his superiors. Their evidence has been discarded by the Tribunals by 
observing that in the absence of independent evidence, the statements of the workmen who were present at the scene 
of occurrence could not be believed. Industrial Tribunal tell in error in discarding the evidence produce by the 
management only because the independent witnesses were not produce them. It is possible that at the time of 
occurrence, only the workers of the Management and the persons who were truing to put up the constructions 
dependent evidence was available. Statements of the fellow workmen had established the misconduct of the 
Respondent. Enquiry officer accepted the testimony of the witness produced by the management who had clearly 
implicated the Respondent. It was a legitimate conclusion which could be arrived at and it would not be open to the 
industrial Tribunal to substitute the said opinion by its own opinion. 


19. Tribunal has set aside the report of the enquiry Officer and the order of dismissal passed by the punishing 
Authority by observing that the charges against the Respondent were not proved beyond reasonable doubt. It has 
repeatedly had been held by the court that the acquittal in a criminal case could not operate as a bar for drawing up 
of a disciplinary proceeding against a delinquent. It is well settled principle of law that yardstick and standard proof 
in a criminal case is different from the one disciplinary proceeding. While the standard of proof in a criminal case is 
proof beyond all reasonable doubt, the standard of proof in a departmental proceeding is preponderance of 
probabilities.” 


Further, the Honorable Supreme Court has observed that in a case where two views are possible on the 
evidence on record, then the Industrial Tribunal should be very slow in coming to a conclusion other than the one 
arrived at by the domestic Tribunal, by substituting its opinion in place of the opinion of the domestic tribunal. 


Thus, in view of the law laid down by the apex court, as discussed above, the plea of the petitioner that 
there is no legal evidence on record is untenable, as there is sufficient evidence on record of the domestic inquiry to 
prove the guilt of the workman in the alleged misconduct. 


18. Further, as regard the appreciation and evaluation of the evidence in matter of domestic inquiry, Hon’ble 
Supreme Court, in the case of State of Rajasthan and others Vs Him Singh, Civil Appeal Number 3340 of 2020, 
date of decision: 29th October 2021, has laid down the principles extracted as here under: - 


“Disciplinary enquiries have to abide by the rules of natural justice. But they are not governed by strict rules of 
evidence which apply to judicial proceedings. The standard of proof is hence not the strict standard which governs a 
criminal trial, of proof be yond reasonable doubt, but a civil standard governed by a preponderance of probabilities. 
Within the rule of preponderance, there are varying approaches based on context and subject. The first end of the 
spectrum is founded on deference and autonomy -deference to the position of the disciplinary authority as a fact- 
finding authority and autonomy of the employer in maintaining discipline and efficiency of the service. Al the other 
end of the spectrum is the principle that the court has the jurisdiction to interfere when the findings in the enquiry 
are based on no evidence or when they suffer from perversity. 


To determine whether the finding in a disciplinary inquiry is based on some evidence an initial or threshold level of 
scrutiny is undertaken. That is to satisfy the conscience of the courts that there is some evidence to support the 
charge of misconduct and to guard against perversity, but this does not allow the court to re- appreciate evidentiary 
findings in a disciplinary enquiry or to substitute a view which appears lo the judge to be more appropriate. To do so 
would offend the first principle which has been outlined above. The ultimate guide is the exercise of robust common 
sense without which the judges' craft is in vain.” 


19. In the case of Hombe Gouda Education Trust Vs State of Karnataka, 2006 SCC, page 430: Hon’ble Supreme 
Court have held that assaulting a superior at a workplace amount to an act of gross indiscipline. The respondent is a 
teacher. Even under grave provocation, a teacher is not expected to abuse the head of the institution in a filthy

language and assault him with a chappal. punishment of dismissal from service, therefore, cannot be said to be 
wholly disproportionate so as to shock one's conscience. Further, Hon’ble Supreme Court held that a person, when 
dismissed from service, is put to great hardship, but that would not mean that a grave misconduct (assault on 
superior at workplace) should go unpunished. Maintenance of discipline of an institution is equally important. 


20.Further, In the case of MP Electricity Board Vs Jagdish Sharma, 2005 SCC, page 401, Hon’ble Supreme Court 
have held: 


"9. In the case on hand, the employee has been found guilty of hitting and injuring his superior officer at the 
workplace obviously in the breach of Presence of other employees This clearly amounted in an discipline in the 
organisation Discipline at the workplace organisation like the employer herein, is the sine qua non for the efficient 
working of the organisation, when an employee breaches such discipline and the employer terminates his services it 
is not open to a Labour Court of an Industrial Tribunal to take view that the punishment awarded is shockingly 
disproportionate to the charge proved. We have already 


referred to the views of this Court. To quote Jack Chan, 


‘Discipline is a form of civilly responsible behaviour which helps maintain social order and contributes to 
the preservation, if not advancement, of collective interests of society at large.’ 


Obviously, this idea is more relevant in considering the working of an organisation like the employer herein or an 
industrial undertaking. Obedience to authority in a workplace is not slavery. It is rot violative of one's natural rights. 
It is essential for the prosperity of the organisation as well as that of its employee’s. When in such a situation, a 
punishment of termination is awarded for hitting and injuring a superior officer supervising the work of the 
employee, with no extenuating circumstance established, it cannot be said to be not justified. It cannot certainly be 
termed unduly harsh or disproportionate. The Labour Court and the High Court in this case totally misdirected 
themselves while exercising their jurisdiction. The Industrial Court made the correct approach and came to the right 
conclusion." 


21. Further, in the case of Ajit Kumar Nag Vs Indian Oil Corporation Limited, 2005 SCC page 764, the 
Honorable Supreme Court has held, in a three-judge bench, in paragraph 56, "It is well settled that the burden 
of proving malafide is on the person making the allegation, and the burden is very heavy. There is every 
presumption in favor of the administration that the power has been exercised bona fide and in good faith. It is to be 
remembered that the allegations of malafide are often more easily made than made out, and the very seriousness of 
such allegations demands proof of a high degree of credibility." 


Further, Hon’ble Supreme Court held that assault, intimidation are penal offences. A workman indulging 
in commission of criminal offenses should not be spared only because he happens to be a union leader. The act does 
not encourage indiscipline. It will be a matter of some concern if the opinion of the inquiry officer can be totally 
ignored, despite the fact that the management is precluded from adducing any fresh evidence before the labor court. 
A union leader does not enjoy immunity from being proceeded with in a case of misconduct. 


22. Inthe case of D. Mulchandani Electric and Radio Industries Limited Vs Workman, 1975 Supreme Court Cases 
page 731, Hon’ble Supreme Court have held: 


establishment 


“Tt was not disputed before us that the allegation of assault, if proved, would be an act subversive of discipline: what 
was contended on behalf of the respondent was between Thana and the premises was that the alleged assault having 
taken place in the train Mulund which was obviously outside the or precincts of the establishment, was not covered 
by Standing Order. 


24(1). The Labour Court also found that the alleged assault did not In our amount to misconduct under Standing 
Order 24(1) which, it was held was restricted to acts and omissions inside the premises of the establish opinion, Lon 
a plain reading of the clause, the words "within the premises or precincts of the establishment" refer not to the place 
where the act which is subversive of discipline or good behaviour is committed but where the consequence of such 
an act manifests itself. In other words, an act, wherever committed, if it has the effect of sub- verting discipline or 
good behaviour within the premises or precincts of the establishment, will amount to misconduct under Standing 
Order 24(1) We are unable to agree that Standing Order 2401) leaves out of its scone an act committed outside 
though it may result in subversion of discipline or good behaviour within the premises or precincts of the 
establishment in question. Such a construction in our view would be quite unreasonable.” 


23. In the case of State bank of Bikaner and Jaipur vs Nemi Channel via 2011 Supreme Court cases page 580 
Hon’ble Supreme Court have held that subsequent acquittal by criminal court will not in any way render completed 
discipline proceeding invalid, nor affect the validity of finding of the guilt and consequential punishment. 


24. Thus, in view of the foregone discussion and_ law laid down by the apex court as discussed above, in the instant 
matter all the charges framed and proved in domestic inquiry against the workman being serious and grave in nature

and stands proved by oral and documentary evidence recorded and produced bin the inquiry. Further, the evidence 
produced by the management before inquiry is legal and admissible as per principle of preponderance of probability 
laid down by Hon’ble Supreme Court in its various decisions as discussed in preceding paragraph of this Award. 
Therefore, order of dismissal of Petitioner workman cannot be faulted with, nor it can be said to be in any way 
disproportionate to the gravity of the charges. Thus, the punishment of dismissal of the workman is proportionate to 
the gravity of the charges, and hence deserve to be upheld. Thus, the action of the respondent management in 
dismissing the services of the workman is held legal and justified. 


This issue is decided against the workman and in favor of the respondent management. 
Issue No: IV 


In view of foregone discussion and finding given at issue No. I, II and III, I am of the considered opinion that the 
action of Respondent management in dismissing the Petitioner from service vide order dated 27-05-2016 is legal 
and justified. Therefore, no interference warrants in the punishment of dismissal order dated 27-05-2016 of the 
Petitioner and the action of Respondent Management is held legal and justified and liable to be confirmed.

In view of the foregone discussion and finding given at issue No. I, II, HI, and IV, the action of Respondent 
Management in dismissing the service of the Petitioner workman vide order dated 27-05-2016 is held legal and

G.S.R. 184.—In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (1) read with clauses (a) and (b) of sub- 
section (2) of section 165 of the Assam Rifles Act 2006 (47 of 2006) and in supersession of the Assam Rifles (Group 
‘C’ combatised posts) Recruitment Rules, 2000, in so far as it relates to the post of Naib Subedar (Pharmacist); and 
the Assam Rifles (Group ‘B’ combatised posts) Recruitment Rules, 2001, in so far as they related to the post of 
Subedar Major (Pharmacist), Subedar (Pharmacist), except as respects to things done or omitted to be done before 
such supersession, the Central Government hereby makes the following rules regulating the method of recruitment to 
the posts of Subedar Major (Pharmacist), Subedar (Pharmacist) and Naib Subedar (Pharmacist), in the Assam Rifles 
in the Ministry of Home Affairs, namely:- 


1. Short title and commencement. — (1) These rules may be called the Ministry of Home Affairs, Assam 
Rifles,Subedar Major (Pharmacist), Subedar (Pharmacist) and Naib Subedar (Pharmacist), Group ‘B’ Posts, 
Recruitment Rules 2025.. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. Application. - These rules shall apply to the posts as specified in column (1) of the Scheduled annexed to 
these rules. 


3: Number of posts, classification and level in the pay matrix. — The number of the said posts, their 
classification and level in pay matrix attached thereto shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the saidSchedule. 


4. Method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications, etc. - The method of recruitment, age-limit, 
qualifications and other matters relating to the said posts shall be as specified in columns (5) to (13) of the said 
Schedule. 


5. Disqualification. — No person, — 
(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 


(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, shall be 
eligible for appointment to the said post: 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal 
law applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, exempt 
any person from the operation of this rule. 


6. Superannuation.-(1) Every person appointed under these rules shall retire from service on the afternoon of 
the last day of the month in which he or she attains the age of sixty years or as prescribed by the Central Government 
from time to time: 


Provided that a person whose date of birth is on the first day of the month, shall retire from service in the 
afternoon of the last day of the preceding month on attaining the age of superannuation. 


(2) No person shall be granted extension in service beyond the prescribed age of retirement on 
superannuation as specified in sub-rule (1). 


7. Power to relax. — Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, 
it may, by order and for reasons to be recorded in writing and in consultation with the Union Public Service 
Commission, relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any class or category of persons. 


Saving. — Nothing in these rules shall affect reservation, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions required to be 


provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, the Other Backward Classes,Ex-servicemen and other special 


categories of persons in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government from time to time in this regard

G.S.R. 185.—In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution and in 
supersession of the Central Bureau of Investigation, Data Entry Operator, Grade ‘A’ posts, Recruitment Rules, 2003, 
except as respects things done or omitted to be done before such supersession, the President, hereby makes the 
following rules regulating the method of recruitment to the post of Data Entry Operator, Grade ‘A’ in the Central 
Bureau of Investigation, namely:- 


1. Short title and commencement.- (1) These rules may be called the Central Bureau of Investigation, Data 
Entry Operator, Grade ‘A’ post, Recruitment Rules, 2025. 

(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 
2. Number of posts, classification and level in pay matrix.- The number of the said post, its classification and 


the level in the pay matrix attached thereto shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the Schedule annexed to these 
10165. 


3. Method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications etc.- The method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications 
and other matters relating to the said post shall be as specified in columns (5) to (13) of the said Schedule. 
4. Disqualifications.- No person,- 
(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 
(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person. 
shall be eligible for appointment to the said post: 
Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal 


law applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, exempt 
such person from the operation of this rule. 


5. Power to relax.- Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, it 
may, by order and for reasons to be recorded in writing, relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any 
class or category of persons. 


6. Saving.- Nothing in these rules shall affect reservations, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions 
required to be provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, the Other Backward Classes, the ex- 
Servicemen and other special categories of persons in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government 
from time to time in this regard.

G.S.R. 186.—In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution, the 
President hereby makes the following rules regulating the method of recruitment to the post of Clinical Embryologist 
in the Ministry of Health and Family welfare, Lady Hardinge Medical College and Smt. Sucheta Kriplani Hospital, 
New Delhi, namely:- 


1. Short title and commencement. - (1) These rules may be called the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Lady 
Hardinge Medical College and Smt. Sucheta Kriplani Hospital, New Delhi, Clinical Embryologist, Group ‘A’ post, 
Recruitment Rules, 2025. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. Number of post, classification and level in pay matrix. - The number of the said post, its classification and level 
in the pay matrix attached thereto, shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the Schedule annexed to these rules. 

3. Method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications, etc. -The method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications and 
other matters relating to the said post shall be as specified in columns (5) to (13) of the said Schedule.

may, by order and for reasons to be recorded in writing and in consultation with the Union Public Service 
Commission, relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any class or category of persons. 

6. Saving. - Nothing in these rules shall affect reservation, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions required to

G.S.R. 187.—In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution and in 
supersession of the All India Institute of Hygiene and Public Health, Calcutta (Group 'C’) Recruitment Rules, 1990, 
in so far as they relate to the post of Museum Curator, Technician Cine-Technician, Assistant Cine-Technician, 
Museum Assistant except as respects things done or omitted to be done before such supersession, the President hereby 
makes the following rules regulating the method of recruitment to the posts of Museum Curator, Technician Cine- 
Technician, Assistant Cine-Technician, Museum Assistant in the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, All India 
Institute of Hygiene and Public Health, Kolkata, namely:- 


1. Short title and commencement. - (1) These rules may be called the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, All 
India Institute of Hygiene and Public Health, Kolkata Museum Curator, Technician Cine-Technician, Assistant 
Cine-Technician, Museum Assistant (Group ‘C’ posts) Recruitment Rules, 2022. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. Number of posts, classification and level in pay matrix. - The number of the said posts, their classification and 
level in the pay matrix attached thereto, shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the schedule annexed to these 
rules. 


3. Method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications, etc.- The method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications and 
other matters relating thereto shall be as specified in columns (5) to (13) of the said Schedule. 


4. Disqualification. — No person, - 
(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person having a spouse living, or 
(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, 
shall be eligible for appointment to the said post: 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal law 
applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, exempt any 
person from the operation of this rule. 


5. Power to relax. - Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, it may 
by order and for reasons to be recorded in writing, relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any 
class or category of persons.

बचाव के लिए मौजूद सड़कें बहुत संकरी थीं। श्री अमरनाथ मिश्रा तुरंत घटनास्थल पर पहुंचे और उन्होंने इलाके को खाली कराना शुरू किया। 
इसके बाद, कुछ स्थानीय स्वयंसेवकों की मदद से उन्होंने प्रभावित क्षेत्र की घेराबंदी की। फिर, वे तुरंत उस इमारत की चौथी मंजिल की ओर दौड़े, 
जहां आग लगी थी। उन्होंने मुख्य लाइन से इमारत की बिजली की आपूर्ति काटी और मकान मालिक श्री सुधाकर के परिवार के सभी सदस्यों को 
घटनास्थल से सकुशल निकालकर इमारत के बाहर एक सुरक्षित स्थान पर पहुंचाया। जिस कमरे से आग फैली थी वहां जहरीला धुआं भरा हुआ 
था। उन्होंने अपनी नाक पर एक रूमाल रखकर उस घर में प्रवेश किया। उन्होंने देखा कि रसोई में आग लगी है, जहां दो एलपीजी गैस सिलेंडर 
रखे हुए थे। अगर सिलेंडरों में आग लग जाती, तो स्थिति और भी भयावह हो सकती थी। उन्होंने तुरंत दोनों सिलेंडरों को घर से बाहर निकालकर 
सुरक्षित स्थान पर रखा और आग पर बालटी से पानी डालना शुरू किया। कुछ ही देर में, घर में लगी आग बुझा दी गई। श्री अमरनाथ मिश्रा की 
सजगता और त्वरित निर्णय लेने की क्षमता के कारण, आग पर जल्द ही काबू पा लिया गया और कोई हताहत नहीं हुआ। 


इस ऑपरेशन में, उत्तर प्रदेश गृह रक्षक एवं नागरिक सुरक्षा सेवा के श्री अमरनाथ मिश्रा, चीफ वार्डन ने अदम्य वीरता, साहस और 
उच्चकोटि की कर्तव्यपरायणता का परिचय दिया।

Statement of service for which the decoration has been awarded 


On 8th February 2023, based on a reliable input about one group of ULFA (I) extremist taking shelter at Malu Gaon 
Hills, Ledo under Margherita Police station with an intention to cause sabotage activities; an operation was launched led by 
IGP, NER along with SP Tinsukia Gurav Abhijit Dilip, IPS, SDPO Margherita Hemanta Kumar Boro, Constable Akhil Ranjan 
Das along with Police team. The police team proceeded to the area at around 9.00 PM and reached to the hills at midnight. 
After detailing cover party in strategic locations, the police team while climbing up the hills to recce the area, an extremist 
group camping on the upper elevation, started indiscriminate fire upon them, however the team managed to duck in the hilly 
terrain without hurt. Thereafter, the police team coordinated accompanying team and approached closer to the extremists in 
spite of heavy fire. When the exact position of the extremists was ascertained, the police team retaliated the fire with aggressive 
support of accompanying team, thereby a fierce exchange of fire ensued and which was lasted for |5-20 minutes. Though the 
exchange of fire was stopped yet the police team remained in lying position for sometimes. But when sound of groaning of a 
person was heard, the police team crawled up to the place and saw an injured extremist, armed with AK rifle in lying position. 
The injured extremist was lifted and rushed to Margherita FRU, Hospital for treatment. In the hospital, doctor on duty declared 
him brought dead. The deceased was later identified as Udoy Axom @ Uddhab Lahon, an Operation Commander of United 
Liberation Front of Assam (Independent). Rest of the extremists managed to flee. A thorough search of the area was conducted 
in the first light where arms, ammunitions and materials were recovered. 


It is to be mentioned that during the operation it was completely dark, rainy and the terrain was difficult to navigate, 
despite of all the odds, the operation resulted in success cheerily for meticulous planning, tactical approach, courage and 
leadership displayed by SP Gurav Abhiyit Dilip, IPS, SDPO Hemanta Kumar Boro and Constable Akhil Ranjan Das. 


In this operation, S/Shri Gurav Abhiit Dilip, IPS, Superintendent of Police, Hemanta Kumar Boro, Sub Divisional 
Police Officer and Akhil Ranjan Das, Constable of Assam Police displayed conspicuous gallantry, courage and devotion to 
duty of a higher order. 


The Medal for Gallantry (GM) is conferred under President’s Secretariat Notification No. 85-Pres/2023 dated 
l4th October, 2023 and Ministry of Home Affairs’ communication No. !024/06/2023-PMA dated l6th October, 2023. 
Consequently, this award carries with it the admissible monetary allowance with effect from 09/02/2023.

Statement of service for which the decoration has been awarded 


On 6-07-206, Shri Babu Ram, IPS, SP Aurangabad got indulgence about camping of an armed group of Maoists 
led by their Commander BJSAC Member Sandeep jee and others in nearby areas of Langurahi yillage situated in 
Chhakarbandha forest under Madanpur PS, with intention to execute some explosive plan. 


Chbakrabandha forest the most infamous den of Maoists, is sprawled in Aurangabad and Gaya districts of Bihar. All 
kachcha tracks are prone to IEDs placed on tactical locations along the heights of both sides of these tracks. These heights 
provide safe cover to Maoists to fire on security forces, whereas security forces have no choice but to pass through these risky 
zones to reach targeted locations to engage Maoists. 


To plan the operation, a joint meeting was held in the office of the SP. It was decided to launch the joint ops in the 
night of !7.07.206 under leadership of the SP Shrl Babu Ram who had decided to participate in the ops himself. A joint team 
consisting of District Police Force Aurangabad and four teams of cobra 205 battalion with their respective Commanders was 
constituted immediately under overall leadership of SP Babu Ram in order to apprehend the Maoists and to defy their nefarious 
plan. Two cobra teams No. | and |2 started from Madanpur at about 0:30 PM same day and after crossing thick forests, 
treacherous trenches and flooded rivers on foot in rainy dark night reached the destination at about 06:30 AM. The other two 
teams l4 & |8 also reached at their positions. Despite a long and constant ambush and search, no movement or trace of Maoists 
was found. Then all the teams moved one by one in east direction towards Dumri Nala. At about l:5 AM on 8-07-20I6 
when Shri Babu Ram with his two teams crossed the Dumri Nala, and the other two teams met a sudden series of Landmines 
blasts followed by a heavy gunshot fire. Some jawans had been Injured badly in the blast. At the same time, Maoists started 
firing on the team led by SP Babu Ram. He Immediately directed other team leader to take his team to help the teams stranded 
in Nala to evacuate and team led by SP Babu Ram retaliated to the enemy with a heavy fire to dominate them. 


Though engulfed in Incessant and iindiscriminate fire, SP Babu Ram along with his team, took tactical position 
immediately and motivated his Jawans to retaliate the enemy with full capacity. Under a strategic decision, the SP without 
caring for bullets of enemy and for his life and showing exemplary courage, maneuvered to the left side of the attack and told 
team member to attack the right flank. The Maoists, sensing that they were being commered, accelerated their firings to the full 
extent. CT Ravi Kumar crawled ahead, amidst the firing and fired upon enemy bravely when he got a bullet injury. The SP 
directed team member to take care of the injured Jawan and he himself along with his district force commandos advanced close 
to the enemy taking tactical cover of boulders and began to fire on the enemy from close distance. This gallant act resulted in 
breakage of Maoist ambush. CT Surendra Paswan, CT Vikas Kumar and CT Sanjay Kumar Choudhary exhibited exemplary 
courage. They without caring of the danger and firing from the enemy, kept advancing towards the enemy and fired on the 
enemy simultaneously. CT Surender Paswan despite being injured, advanced with the SP amid heavy firing. The enemy was 
in a dominating position and firing continuously. Our jawans being at lower position could not take aim at the top of the hill. 
Despite all odds and challenges the enemy was posing, the SP despite himself being injured, enthusing the morale of his Jawans, 
motivated them to capture the hill top without exposing themselves to the enemy's eye sight. Under the tactical leadership of 
the SP, the team taking covers of boulders succeeded in approaching the target, i.e. top of the hill under effective support of 
cover fire. The teams having approached the target, positioned themselves and discharged heavy fire on Maoists group under 
the command of SP Babu Ram. This befitting reply with utmost courage and absolute determination pushed the Maoists back 
and they fled away with their injured and killed members under the cover of IED blasts leaving three dead bodies of their 
accomplices, ammunitions in huge quantity, IEDs, explosives and other belongings. 


On other side, teams stranded in Nala also showed exemplary courage. Despite being injured SI Tarbabu Yadav and 
SI Ram Raj Singh in coordination with Cobra teams retaliated the enemy bravely and with strong determination in order to 
suppress their fire power, and evacuated the injured jawans regardless of the risk to their lives. This courageous counter attack 
by the police team broke the ambush laid by the Maoists and forced them to fled away. Uncaring for his personal safety, SI 
Saket Saurabh actively participated in the process of removal of injured Jawans to a safe place despite the attack made by the 
Maoists. 


In the face of prevailing apprehension of landmines laid by the Maoists on track along Dumri Nala, the only exit route 
and probability of presence of their armed groups on hilltop in way, the SP Aurangabad displaying remarkable professional 
skill with indomitable spirit and outstanding leadership evacuated seven injured jawans safely from the ambush site making 
cross country movement. 


In this operation, S/Shri Babu Ram, IPS, Superintendent of Police, Saket Saurabh, Sub-Inspector, Ram Raj Singh, 
Sub-Inspector, Tarbabu Yadav, Sub-Inspector, Sanjay Kumar Choudhary, Constable, Surendra Paswan, Constable and Vikas 
Kumar, Constable of Bihar Police displayed conspicuous gallantry, courage and devotion to duty of a higher order.

Statement of service for which the decoration has been awarded 


Bhejji Area of Sukma District is considered to be the stronghold of CPI (Maoists). Due to its geographical features 
with the presence of heavy dense forests, wide ranges of hills and a number of small streams, it turns to be the hiding zone for 
the Maoists. Inputs regarding the presence of 35-40 naxals in the Danteshpuram area of PS Bhejji is regularly received with 
this background. 


On receiving specific inputs from reliable sources, an anti-naxal operation was launched at around 8.0 hrs. on 
07.05.2023 from PS Errabore under the leadership of Shri Sunil Sharma, IPS, SP, Sukma. In order to ensure the proper 
execution of the plan Shri Sunil Sharma, SP Sukma himself briefed the operation party regarding die intelligence inputs and 
the proper execution of the plan. This team after proper briefing, along with requisite arms and ammunitions and 
communication equipment, headed towards villages of Pantabhejji, Mailasur and Danteshpuram. 


Meanwhile, the team commander Shri Sunil Sharma, as per the plan, launched the supporting parties. The first team 
of 202 CoBRA Bn marched from Kolaiguda to Village Gachchanpalli. The second party of 50th Bn of CRPF marched from 
Elarmadgu to village Mailasur-Bhodrajpadar and the third party being of 2l9th Bn of CRPF marched from Kottacheru to 
village Bhandarpadar. 


The operation route was through the villages of Pantabhejji, Mailasur and Danteshpuram. After reaching the target 
area and accessing the scenario, Shri Sunil Sharma gave further instruction to the team and encouraged the party to move 
forward. At around 05:30 hrs. in the morning, the party taking proper cover started returning along cross-country route, 
suddenly an indiscriminate firing was opened upon the police personnel by around 35-40 naxal cadres, wearing black uniform 
and ununifonned dress of banned PLGA Battalion. The enemy party had sophisticated automatic weapons and equipments. 
The aim of this attack was to kill police personnel and to loot their weapons and ammunitions. The Security personnel took 
position and warned the naxals to stop the firing and urged them to surrender. However, in response to the pleas to surrender; 
the naxals started attacking even more vigorously. Consequently, the police party had no other option but to reciprocate in self 
defence. During the course of this attack, the team leader Shri Sunil Sharma, marching tactically forward, directed one team 
member to cordon from the right direction and directed DRG Commander SI Sandeep Kumar Madile to cordon from the left 
direction. Shri Sunil Sharma with his team headed towards the naxals and tried to push back. All the parties moved forward, 
fire and started encircling the Maoists with exemplary courage and leading from the front. They kept on encouraging the police 
personnel to give fitting reply to the Maoists. Meanwhile naxals continued the attack with automatic weapons. 


Realizing the sudden aggression by the police party, the Maoists retreated taking the advantage of thick forest cover 
and nearby hillocks. After the fierce gun battle which lasted for around 35-40 minutes, the whole area was thoroughly searched 
and teams recovered 0] uniformed male body and 0! ununiformed female body along with one 303 rifle with magzing having 
one live bullet along with daily use items. The party also recovered 0! No. naxal made BGL Cell, 0l SLR magazine loaded 
with 8 live rounds. During the search operation in attack area, the security personnel recovered !0 blank rounds of AK-47 
rifle, 02 blank rounds of 303 rifle, 05 blank rounds of SLR rifle, 03 blank rounds of INSAS rifle and from the attacking spot of 
police party recovered blank rounds-2lof AK-47 rifle and 06 blank rounds of SLR rifle. 


During police naxal encounter, naxals fired around 200-300 rounds upon security personnel whereas security 
personnel fired 357 rounds from AK-47, |l8 rounds from SLR, 23 rounds from INSAS and along with 05 nos. of UBGL. 


In this operation, S/Shri Sunil Sharma, IPS, Superintendent of Police, Sandeep Kumar Madile, Sub-Inspector and 
Madkam Pandu, Constable of Chhattisgarh Police displayed conspicuous gallantry, courage and devotion to duty of a higher 
order.

through the villages Chimli, Nilgod, Mekalguda and Pulampad. After thoroughly searching the whole area, the party moved 
tactically towards the task. On |2.08.2020 at around 06.30 hrs while the party was marching in between the forest of Pulampad 
and Mekalguda, an indiscriminate firing was opened upon the DRG and DEF Police personnel by around 40-50 naxal cadres, 
wearing black uniforms and ununiformed dress of banned PLGA Battalion bearing sophisticated automatic weapons and 
equipment. This attack aimed to kill police personnel and loot their weapons and ammunition. The Security personnel took 
position and warned the naxals to stop the firing and urged them to surrender. However in response to pleas to surrender, the

Commander Nanda Markam and directed him to cordon from the right direction and directed another DRG Commander Umesh 
Markam to cordon from the left direction. SI Mukesh Patel along with his team headed towards the naxals and tried to push 
them back. All the parties moved forward and retaliated tactically to the naxal attack. Meanwhile, naxals continued the attack 
with automatic weapons and used BGL upon the Security personnel. 


The Security personnel followed the naxals for about I.5 km to 2.0 km. Seeing the aggressive approach of security 
personnel, the naxals ran away into the jungle. Aftermath when the security personnel launched the Cordan and search 
operation, the naxals executed a surprise attack upon them. In response, the security forces took position and retaliated. Due to 
the quick response by SI Mukesh Patel, Constable Madkam Hadma, Constable Madkam Deva, Constable Barse Hunga and 
Auxiliary Constable Roshan Gupta, naxals failed in the plan to break the ambush. Realizing the aggression by the police party, 
the Maoists retreated taking advantage of thick forest cover and nearby hillocks.

recovered 02 uniformed male bodies and 02 ununiformed male bodies along with 0l No. 303 rifles (04 nos. live bullets), 03 
nos. Bharmar rifle, 0! desi bomb along with daily used items. During the search operation in the attack area, the security 
personnel recovered 05 blank rounds of AK-47, 04 blank rounds of SLR rifle, 03 blank rounds of Insas rifle and 06 blank 
rounds of 303 rifle. 


During the Police naxal encounter, naxals fired around 450-500 rounds upon security personnel whereas security 
personnel fired 9]8 rounds along with 0 HE bomb and 03 Nos. of UBGL. 

Later the dead naxal were identified as Bhogam Bhima S/o Bhogam 0५9, 30 years old (member of platoon no 0),

coy member) and Nuppo Deva S/o Nuppo Bhima, 28 years old (Militia coy member). 

In this operation, S/Shri Madkam Hadma, Constable, Madkam Deva, Constable, Barse Hunga, Constable and Roshan

equipments. The aim of this attack was to kill police personnel and to loot their weapons and ammunitions. The naxal attacked 
from all directions and also fired from motar shells upon the police party. The security personnel took position and warned the 
naxals to stop the firing and urge them to surrender. However in response to pleas to surrender, the naxals started attacking 
even more vigorously. Consequently, the police party had no other option but to fire in self defence. During the course of this 
attack, Commander of DRG Burkapal 2 and Commander of DRG Chintagufa along with their team communicated with other 
back parties about the firing. The other team forwarded towards the EOF area by encircling the area from right direction and 
at the same time team of ASI Nanda Madkam with TI Shankar Lal Dhruw encircled from left direction. Both the parties 
tactically moved forward while firing the naxals. DRG Burkapal 2 and Chintagufa 2 was being fired upon by naxal from three 
different directions. All the parties were retaliating to the naxal attack. Meanwhile naxals continued the attack with automatic 
weapons and used BGL upon the Security personnel.

arms and ammunitions of one martyr. 


The martyred Police Personnel showed utter disregard to personnel safety and wellbeing while they had the option to 
retreat to higher ground. The martyrs laid down their lives and kept firing despite the numerical superiorly of the enemy and in 
face of death. Blood spots and tail signs of bodies being dragged were also found on various locations. During the aforesaid 
attack, surrendered naxal cadres present in the police party identified some naxal leaders in the attack as Hidma- battalion 
commander, Sonu- PLGA company no. | commander, Nagesh- PLGA company no. 2 commander, Jaiman madvi, Sannu,

Army CO 42 RR. After meticulously chalking out a plan and taking into consideration all possible hostilities, a joint cordon 
was laid by Police Kupwara, Police Awantipora and Army 42 RR at village Hardumir Tral. The composite party of Army 42

maintaing high level of surprise till gap free cordon get established. After laying & strengthening the cordon, the steps for 
search of terrorists in the target house was started by the joint team of Police Kupwara led by SSP Yougal Kumar & Police 
Awantipora led by SP Mohd Yousif alongwith ASI Parmeet Singh, HC Farooq Ahmad Awan, Ct. Safeer Lone, Follower 
Ghulam Jeelani Gojar (Deedad) & others with the assistance of Army 42 RR. 


On sensing the movement of forces, the terrorists hiding in the target house started indiscriminate firing upon them so 
as to break the cordon and get escaped from the cordoned area. But due to the presence of mind, search party who were 
searching in the target house, quickly took positions and retaliated in self-defense, thus foiled the attempt of hiding terrorists 
to escape from the cordoned area. As such the presence & exact location of the terrorist was confirmed, the cordon was

one led by SSP Yougal Kumar along with Ct. Safeer Lone, Follower Ghulam Jeelani Gojar (Deedad) & party of counterparts

house was located in the built-up area and there was every apprehension of eruption of law & order problem and in order to 
thwart any such attempt, the deployment of Police Awantipora and Police Kupwara was strategically made at the points in its 
surroundings so as to sterile the target house/area from any kind of extrinsic interference which might otherwise could have 
disrupted to carry out the anti-terrorist operation successfully. 


Since conducting the operation in broad day light is always full of challenges that too when reports of hiding of local 
terrorists is received. SSP Kupwara acted as per the situation on ground, revisited the strategy and advised SSP Mohammad 
Yousif to follow his team from two different directions for safe evacuation of civilians from the target house and from the 
houses falling in close proximity of the target house. This was a sensitive and vital stage of the operation to evacuate the 
civilians who were trapped in the target house and the adjoining houses, as there was every apprehension of attack from the 
besieged terrorists. The dare devil task was conducted by SSP Yougal Kumar alongwith HC Farooq Ahmad Awan, Ct. Safeer 
Lone, Follower Ghulam Jeelani Gojar (Deedad) amid the shower of fire from the terrorists. The evacuation of civilians was 
made possible with the help of covering fire provided by Police component Tral & Army 42 RR. After that, hiding terrorists

spearheaded by SSP Yougal Kumar alongwith HC Farooq Ahmad Awan, Ct. Safeer Lone, Follower Ghulam Jeelani Gojar 
(Deedad) took cover and fought bravely from the front without caring for their lives and neutralized the said terrorists inside

Koil Shikargah Tral and Rahi Rasool Bhat @ Adil (Category “B”) S/o Gh. Rasool Bhat R/o Kanipora Dadasara Awantipora,

terrorists. Case FIR No. 55/202 U/S 307, 7/27 I.A.Act, 8, 9, 38 & 39 ULA(P) Act stands registered in P/S Tral.

S/Shri 

l. Rayees Ahmad Ganie SgCT GM 

2, Ummar Majid Mir Constable GM 


Statement of service for which the decoration has been awarded 


On 02.02.2022, Police Shopian generated a specific input about the presence of terrorists in orchard area of Nadigam- 
Nowpora, Shopian. The village Nadigam which has been very vulnerable from terrorism point of view owing to its topography, 
dense orchards, support base to terrorists, as such, conducting of operation in the area was a daunting task for the Police/Security 
forces. The input was promptly shared with CO 34 RR and Commandant |78 Bn CRPF and after thorough deliberation; a joint 
CASO was launched in the target area to flush out the hiding terrorists. 


Accordingly, as per the discussed plan; joint teams of !78 Bn. CRPF, 34 RR and Police Shopian quickly laid the 
cordon under the overall command of Shri Amritpal Singh, IPS, SSP Shopian. As the orchard area was quite bigger and covered 
with heavy snowfall, it was decided to flow the drone in between orchard area of Nadigam-Nowpora village to find out the 
suspected hideout. During the drone monitoring, a suspected hideout was noticed in the orchard area. The hole of the hideout 
was open and an iron door was seen over the hideout. Immediately, all the joint teams were alerted and area was sealed to tight 
the inner cordon. Joint troops of Police Shopian including SgCt. Rayees Ahmad Ganie, Ct. Ummar Majid Mir & others, Army 
34 RR and |78th Bn. CRPF, were ordered to enter into orchard area from all directions and advance as per the plan discussed. 


As the joint forces were advancing towards the suspected hideout, terrorists sensing the movement of security forces 
resorted indiscriminate firing on the initial joint cordon party from good distance and run towards Nadigam adjoining village. 
At this juncture, an appeal was made to terrorists for surrender, but they refused and instead geared-up his speed with firing. 
As the orchard was congested with apple trees and covered with heavy snow, the joint cordon teams advanced tactically towards 
suspected hideout with speed. The fleeing terrorist kept on firing on the joint forces. Finding the distance is getting very close, 
the suspected terrorist heavily fired on the aforesaid joint team who were trying to approach him. At this time, the joint team 
came under heavy fire of suspected terrorist. Despite this attack, the joint team did not lose their concentration and continued 
to advance. This was the deadly attempt taken by the terrorist which showed that he was highly trained to operate the weapon 
during running position in snowy ground and adverse situation. As the terrorist was visual with sophisticated weapon and was 
firing on the joint operational party. In retaliation and using operational skills, joint party of Police Shopian, 34 RR & 78th 
Bn CRPF fired in self-defense. It was impossible to advance with iron shield as ground was covered with heavy snow. The 
joint operational team comprising of DySP Raja Majid Batt, DySP Mohd Ashrif, HC Ayaz Ahmad, SgCt. Shahbaz Ahmad, 
SgCt Rayees Ahmad Ganie, Ct. Mohd Yaseen, SPO Ishfaq Majeed & SPO Mohd Shafi rained the bullets together on the fleeing 
terrorist and neutralized him in their first thrust of retaliation. 


Though, there was no fire from either side after this exchange of fire but there were possibilities of one missing 
suspected terrorist in the cordoned area. Accordingly, a joint search of SFs was initiated to find the other terrorist hiding in 
cordon. An extensive search was carried out by the joint troops but despite combing the cordoned area, nothing was found. 
Then the body of neutralized terrorist was retrieved from encounter site and was identified as Umar Ishfaq Malik S/o Ab Ahad 
Malik R/o Bungam, Shopian. The slain terrorist was functioning as District Commander of Hizbul Mujahideen Terrorist outfit 
and was involved in various terror related incidents. With his elimination, the terrorist network within South Kashmir in general 
and in District Shopian in particular has suffered a major setback. Arms/ammunition was also recovered from the possession 
of slain terrorist. Case FIR No. 0I/2022 U/S 307 IPC, 7/27 I.A.Act, 6 & 20 ULA(P) Act stands registered in P/S Imamsahib 
for further investigation. 


The professionalism coupled with outstanding courage demonstrated by SgCt. Rayees Ahmad Ganie and Ct. Ummar 
Majid Mir while fighting the terrorist without caring for their lives was remarkable as the endeavor to reach to the target in 
extremely hostile situation was truly Gallant. Although, the terrorist tried his best to cause damage the forces by resorting to 
indiscriminate firing in which all they had a very narrow escape. However, they without losing their concentration, fought 
bravely and foiled his nefarious design. 


In this operation, S/Shri Rayees Ahmad Ganie, SgCT and Ummar Majid Mir, Constable of Jammu & Kashmir Police 
displayed conspicuous gallantry, courage and devotion to duty of a higher order. 


The Medal for Gallantry (GM) is conferred under President’s Secretariat Notification No. 85-Pres/2023 dated 
l4th October, 2023 and Ministry of Home Affairs’ communication No. !024/06/2023-PMA dated l6th October, 2023. 
Consequently, this award carries with it the admissible monetary allowance with effect from 02/02/2022. 


(File No. 020/44/2024-PMA)

Statement of service for which the decoration has been awarded 


On 09.03.202l, Shri Mohammad Ameen Bhat, DySP, Sopore received specific information through human source 
regarding presence of terrorist Commander of Al-badr outfit in a residential house at Kanipora Tujjer. Accordingly, DySP 
Mohd Ameen Bhat alongwith his escort personnel did recce of the area to identify the target house and its adjacent area and 
the routes approaching the target house in a Civil Vehicle. After identification of target house, two QRTs of Police Component 
Sopore headed by Inspr. Zia-ur-Rehman and Inspr. Ishfaq Ahmad respectively, one QRT of PC Wadura headed by Insp. 
Parveen Kumar and one QRT of P/S Bomai headed by Insp. Imtiyaz Ahmad SHO P/S Bomai; immediately called to P/S Bomai 
where whole planning for execution of the operation was made and accordingly the suspected area and the target house was 
cordoned off immediately. 


As per the information of human source, the terrorist had to stay in the residential house only for half an hour. All the 
entry and exit routes were plugged off to ensure that the terrorist does not escape from the spot. During the process of cordon, 
the suspicious movement was observed in the already identified target house by the QRT headed by DySP (OPS) Sopore and 
accordingly the information was immediately passed to all other QRTs engaged in the operation. After sometime, the holed- 
up terrorist came out from the residential house and fired indiscriminately upon the QRT headed by DySP (OPS) Sopore and 
in the initial exchange of firing he got injured, however he despite being injured ran and managed his entry in to another 
complex in the vicinity. 


Since some |0-!2 houses were inside the cordon and the inmates of these houses were trapped in their respective 
houses and there were imminent chances of civil causality if the last and final assault is carried out on the very movement. So, 
in order to avert the civilian causality; the QRTs were put to task to evacuate the civilians first and in the endeavor; all the 
trapped civilians at least from l0-2 houses were evacuated to the safe places. After complete evacuation of trapped civilians, 
the cordon was more tightened by resealing all entry and exist routs, the holed-up terrorist was challenged to surrender but he 
instantly turned down the request and fired indiscriminately upon the searching parties which was retaliated immediately and 
effectively retaliated leading to a brief encounter. In the encounter one terrorist of Al-Badr outfit who was lateron identified as 
Chief Commander namely Abdul Gani Khawaja @ Skinder @ Qari Jaleel S/o Mohd Mukhtar Khawaja R/o Kralgund, 
Handwara got killed. Huge quantity of arms/ammunitions was recovered from the possession of slain terrorist. Case FIR No. 
/202 U/S 307 IPC, 7/27 LA.Act stands registered in P/S Bomai. The slain was a hardcore terrorist and since long had 
unleashed a reign of terror among the general people especially Political activists in the jurisdiction of Police District Sopore 
and Handwara by way of killing innocent civilians and was involved in a number of terror actions on security forces and Police. 


It was conspicuous bravery, professionalism and leadership qualities exhibited by DySP Mohd Ameen Bhat, Insp. 
Zia-ur-Rehman and Ct. Gh. Hassan Mir, in the instant operation and their contribution is praiseworthy and gallant by all means. 
This is because of their matchless contribution that one hardcore terrorist commander got eliminated without any collateral 
damage. 


In this operation, S/Shri Mohd Ameen Bhat, Deputy Superintendent of Police, Zia-Ur- Rehman, Inspector and Gh. 
Hassan Mir, Constable of Jammu & Kashmir Police displayed conspicuous gallantry, courage and devotion to duty of a higher 
order. 


The Medal for Gallantry (GM) is conferred under President’s Secretariat Notification No. 85-Pres/2023 dated 
l4th October, 2023 and Ministry of Home Affairs’ communication No. !024/06/2023-PMA dated l6th October, 2023. 
Consequently, this award carries with it the admissible monetary allowance with effect from 09/03/202.

Statement of service for which the decoration has been awarded 


On the intervening night of 2!/22.04.2022, on the basis of credible input regarding presence of two/three Fidayeen 
Pak terrorists of Jaish-e-Mohammad (JeM) terrorist organization in Sunjwan, Jammu area; SP PC Jammu and SSP Jammu 
planned the operation and zeroed in the target area and planned to cordon the suspected Mohalla i.e., Green Valley, Gaziabad, 
Sunjwan and its adjoining area. Inputs suggested that these terrorists are specifically tasked to strike the high value targets and 
disrupt the upcoming VVIP visit in Jammu. 


After proper lying of the cordon, search operation was launched in the area to make sure that the civilians are safe 
without letting the terrorists to break the cordon and flee away. During search at about 0335 hrs, the terrorists doubted that they 
are trapped by the security forces and to show their presence with the intent to create terror by killing the security officials, 
they launched grenade attack on the BP Bunker of SOG Jammu and one Gypsy of police and fired indiscriminately on the 
troops deployed on the ground. During the heavy exchange of fire from both side, one officer of CISF got martyred on spot 
and HC Balraj Singh & SPO Sahil Kumar Sharma, got injured. Sensing the gravity of the situation, Inspr Nayat Ali assisted by 
PSI Mohamad Younis Khanday without caring of their own safety, braved the bullets and reached to the location of martyred 
ASI and evacuated his body. The injured jawans HC Balraj Singh and SPO Sahil Kumar Sharma who were also lying in the 
pool of blood at the encounter site, were evacuated after very hectic efforts by Inspr. Sudhir Sharma and Inspr. Jai Paul Sharma. 
The rescue team showed great courage and bravery in rescuing the injured jawans by braving all the bullets. The timely brave 
action by the rescuing officers was instrumental in saving the precious life of the injured jawans. 


Immediately after evacuation of injured, striking teams were formed. One was led by Naresh Singh, SP PC Jammu 
assisted by DySP Ops Javed Ahmed, DySP Ops Vaseem Mehmood, Inspr. Pawan Singh, Inspr. Arjun Magotra and other 
officials of SOG Jammu, 2nd striking Team was led by SSP Jammu Chandan Kohli assisted by SP Mamta Sharma, Inspr 
Sameer Jelani, ASI Balbir Singh, other officials of district police and also by officials of CRPF and 9 PARA special force. 


In retaliation to the firing of the terrorists, the striking teams counter fired at the terrorists and encounter started and 
firing continued for some time from both the sides. The terrorists were well trained and were carrying huge number of arms & 
ammunitions including IEDs and Grenades. One of the striking teams when fired on the terrorists from high terrain, they took 
the advantage of darkness and run towards an empty house and took shelter in it. The other striking teams cordoned that 
particular house from all sides to foil the plan of terrorists to cause maximum damage to the security forces. 


Both the striking teams were located very close to the house where the terrorists were hiding and were in the firing 
range of terrorists but despite this, the officers/officials displayed utmost courage and bravery in holding their positions and 
retaliated the fire of the terrorists. Both the striking teams were fired upon by the hiding terrorists very heavily with automatic 
weapons, UBGL Grenades as they were desperate and trying to break the cordon and escape from the encounter site but both 
the striking teams retaliated professionally and fight very bravely and tactically. 


ADGP Jammu, Mukesh Singh, IPS and DIG Jammu Kathua Samba Range, Vivek Gupta, IPS were supervising the 
operation at the encounter site and coordinating /leading the troops for achieving the desired results without any collateral 
damage and had given sufficient opportunity to terrorists to surrender and made repeated announcements but the terrorists were 
fidayeens, hardcore and highly trained Foreign Terrorists. By this time, it was clear that these terrorists were completely 
radicalized and have been tasked to carry out fidayeen attack. The striking teams kept on retaliated the fire of the terrorists 
during the night and hold their position till first light in the morning and ensured that terrorist could not break the cordon of the 
security force. 


Finally, the striking teams led by Naresh Singh, SP PC Jammu, Chandan Kohli IPS, SSP Jammu assisted by CRPF 
and 9 PARA carried out the operation to eliminate the terrorists. They were hiding inside the small bathroom which was 
separate from the main house. The terrorists kept on repeatedly firing from inside the bathroom on police party but the Police 
party did not let them escape and kept them contained and engaged inside the bathroom only. The terrorist immediately started 
firing with UBGL and also throw grenades on the vehicle of SP PC Jammu Naresh Singh and the officer had narrow escape. 
Some of the Armor-Piercing (AP) bullets also passed through the BP Gypsy which was just behind the vehicle of SP PC Jammu 
but both the striking parties’ one led by SP PC Jammu and second by SSP Jammu retaliated with full force and subsequently 
they were successful in eliminating two terrorists. 


The operation continued for seven hours and all the hiding terrorists were eliminated in the said operation. During 
search, two dead bodies of unidentified terrorists were recovered from the room alongwith huge quantity of Arms & 
Ammunitions. Accordingly, Case FIR No. 75/2022 UIS 302,307,332,[20-8, I2l- A, IPC, 7 27 l.A.Act, 6,l8 & 20 The 
Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 957 stands registered in P/S Bahu Fort, Jammu for further investigation. 


The whole operation was conducted without an iota of collateral damage only because of the outstanding command 
and control exercised by operational teams conjugated with the display of the rarest of the rare bravery and extreme devotion 
to the duty by them. The members of the operational teams generally and especially Smt. Mamta Sharma, SP South Jammu,

On 0.I0.2023, Shopian Police received a specific intelligence input regarding the presence of terrorists of proscribed 
LeT outfit in village Alishipora under the jurisdiction of P/S Zainapora. As per input, terrorists were in process to carry out 
major terror activities in the area to threaten the general public. On this, Police Shopian launched an operation in collaboration 
with 44 RR & CRPF [780 Bn. under the overall supervision of SSP Tanushree, IPS including DySP Raja Majid Batt and his 
team consisting of HC Khurshid Ahmed, SgCt Shabaz Ahmad Ganai & others alongwith QRTs of 44 RR & CRPF [780॥ Bn 
and moved towards the target area and laid initial cordon. 


During the spot interrogation of a few occupants, one was found a bit nervous; who confirmed presence of two 
suspected terrorists in the residential house No.|2-B at Alishipora. The drone service was used to locate the exact positions of 
hidden terrorists and 02 hidden terrorists were seen at doorstep of house No.l2-B. After getting confirmation of hiding terrorists 
in the targeted house and to avoid any untoward incident, targeted house was covered from different directions. Initially, teams 
consisting of aforesaid police personnel and QRTs of 44 RR & CRPF |78th Bn. were formed to start the search of target area 
to ensure that terrorists could not escape. During search operation, target area was pinpointed/ zeroed by the searching teams. 


In the meantime, terrorists hiding in the house sensing the movement of operational parties opened indiscriminate fire 
upon the searching parties from House No. 2-B with intention to kill them. The search parties immediately took cover and 
retaliated with courage triggering a fierce gunfight between the terrorists and search parties. However, it was noticed that some 
civilians have trapped in the cordon area. It was decided to ensure their evacuation to safe place to prevent any collateral 
damage. The search party of DySP Raja Majid Batt took the responsibility of evacuation of trapped civilians and moved them 
to safer locations. 


Afterwards, Police teams headed by DySP Javeed Ahmad were formed for final assault to eliminate the holed-up 
terrorists. Before launching final assault, besieged terrorists were asked to surrender, which they declined and instead opened 
heavy volume of fire and grenade lobbing towards Police/security forces. 


At this moment, terrorists tried to sneak from target house towards the dense forest but they had no way to escape. 
The dejected terrorists find no option being surrounded by Police/SFs from all sides, decided to challenge the team. One of the 
terrorists haphazardly ran from target house while firing indiscriminately with AK series Rifle towards the South East. The 
terrorist was visual with sophisticated weapon indiscriminately firing on teams of Police/SFs. DySP Javeed Ahmad ordered his 
team to fire together and rained the bullets on the terrorist who was resultantly neutralized. Another terrorist got bullet injures 
and he hid himself and again tried to flee by crawling from cordon. But as the terrorist disclosed his position, he got trapped in 
the firing of Police/ SFs deployed in Darasgah (firebase) and the team lead by DySP Raja Majid Batt and his team alongwith 
QRTs of 44 RR & CRPF [78॥ Bn fired heavily upon the terrorist and neutralized him just ahead of 30-40 meters of target 
house. 


Afterwards, the joint teams carried out thorough search with due precautions to check any other hiding terrorist. 
However, only the bodies of two terrorists along with sophisticated weapons were recovered. The eliminated terrorists were 
later on identified as Marifat Maqbool Mugloo S/o Mohd Maqbool Mugloo R/o Chiegund Keegam, Shopian and Jazim Farooq 
@ Abrar S/o Faroog Ahmad Wani R/o Shirmal Zainapora Shopian (both “B” Category of LeT outfit). Arms/ammunition was

Statement of service for which the decoration has been awarded 


During the intervening night of 27/28.02.2023, Police Awantipora received specific information regarding the 
presence/movement of terrorists in village Padgampora, Awantipora who were conspiring to commit terror act in the area. 
Upon confirmation of input, the operation was planned and coordinated with 55 RR & 30 Bn CRPF for cordon and search. 
The information was also shared with DIG SKR Anantnag. 


As per evolved strategy, the composite party of Police Awantipora, Army 55 RR and CRPF 30 Bn approached the 
target area by adopting the unconventional treacherous routes maintaining high level of surprise till gap free cordon get 
established. After laying & strengthening the cordon, the steps for search of terrorists in the target area was started by the joint 
team of Police Awantipora led by SSP Ajaz Ahmed alongwith DySP Hilal Khaliq Bhat, HC Javid Ahmad Shah, Ct Rayaz 
Ahmad Wani & others wisth Army 55 RR & CRPF 30 Bn. 


When one of the search parties entered Jamia Masjid, they came under heavy volume of fire from the first floor of 
Jamia Masjid. The fire was immediately retaliated by the search party. In the heavy volume of exchange of fire, one terrorist 
got hit and fell down whereas the other managed to escape to one of the nearby residential houses. 


During ensuing gun battle, two army Jawans of 55 RR sustained grievous bullet injuries, who were immediately 
shifted to 92 Base Hospital Srinagar. Among them, one Army Jawan Naik Pawan Kumar succumbed to his injuries and attained 
martyrdom whereas other Army Jawan namely Heam Raj was under treatment and was later stable. 


In view of darkness and chilling cold, it was very tough for security forces to ensure safety of every one and the 
evacuation of injured soldiers was a great challenge amidst the on-going firing. Police, Army 55 RR and CRPF 30 Bn carried 
out thorough search of the Jamia Masjid in which dead body of one terrorist namely Agqib Mushtaq Ahmad Bhat 
R/o Malangpora Pulwama was recovered. He was “A” category terrorist of HM/TRF outfit. 


Since the terrorists were hiding in the Jamia Masjid, there was every apprehension of eruption of law & order problem 
and in order to thwart any such attempt, the deployment of Police Awantipora alongwith major chunk of CRPF 30 Bn under 
the command of DySP Mumtaz Ali and counterpart of CRPF was strategically made at the Padgampora-Malangpora axis near 
the encounter site, whereas Inspr. Younis Khan alongwith CRPF contingent was placed in law & order mode on the rear side 
of the mosque/ Mohalla so as to sterile the target area from any kind of extrinsic interference which otherwise could have 
disrupted to carry out the anti- terrorist operation successfully. 


The other terrorist, however, took shelter in a nearby residential house in the garb of darkness and earlier cover fire 
provided by killed terrorist. The dare devil task was conducted by joint team of Police Awantipora, Army 55 RR and CRPF 
30th Bn spearheaded by DIG SKR Anantnag amid the shower of fire from the terrorist. The evacuation of civilians was 
ensured from the encounter side by party of Police component Awantipora led by DySP Hilal Khaliq Bhat with the help of 
cover fire provided by Police component Awantipora & CRPF 30th Bn. After a brief lull, a quad-copter was pressed into 
service by Army 55 RR to know condition of the terrorist. Images captured by the quad-copter suggested that the terrorist was 
presumably neutralized. This exchange of firing with hold up terrorist continued till afternoon on 28.02.2023. The neutralized 
terrorist was identified as Aijaz Ahmad Bhat S/o Gh. Mohammad Bhat R/o Teli Mohalla Syedabad Aripal Tral. He was 
affiliated with JeM terrorist outfit (Category 7 (7). Arms/ammunition was also recovered from the possession of slain terrorists. 
Case FIR No. 28/2023 U/S 307, 302, 326 IPC, 7/27 LA.Act, l3, 6, 8, 9, 23, 38 & 39 ULA(P) Act stands registered in 
P/S Awantipora for further investigation. 


In the entire operation, DySP Hilal Khaliq Bhat, HC Javid Ahmad Shah and Ct Rayaz Ahmad Wani were oblivious 
to imminent danger but had played a conspicuous role of bravery, courage, rare tactical acumen and exemplary joint

element of surprise for the remaining party. Recognizing the direction of the Naxals' movement, Shri Santosh Kumar Pal, 2 IC, 
directed the buddy Ct Vivek Kumar to advance from the left flank to provide support to Ct Lekhraj Chetiy, who was chasing 
one Naxal. Simultaneously, he instructed the right flank buddy Ct Abhin Kumar Majhi to crawl and position them near the wall

and opened indiscriminate fire in his direction. Fortunately, he narrowly escaped and undeterred by the hail of Naxal fire,
